entries.title: The square integral in the block-joining estimate
entries.locator: arXiv:2011.04642v2, section 2.3, proof of Lemma 2, PDF p. 4; unnumbered integral before (7), HTML equation (12). Versioned HTML and PDF text compared; no visual PDF check.
entries.claim: The displayed square integral is evaluated as log(1 + 2A/(8K)), leading to a joining estimate with numerator 8.
entries.problem: The correct integral is log((8K+A)^2 / (8K(8K+2A))). At A=8K it equals log(4/3), whereas the displayed expression is log 3.
entries.correction: PAFY proves the exact integral and a discrete bound retaining the integer floor. Numerator 64 gives a valid summable bound with the same exponent; enlarge the minimum separation constant. This repairs this estimate only.
entries.leanImpact: Use the corrected integral identity and an explicit integer truncation. The comparison and summable-tail argument are written in PAFY. A complete wiki proof of JZG4 uses only PAFY's integral identity, with its own discrete comparison, and not the source's Lemma 2 numerics. No compiled declaration is supplied. The published theorem is not contradicted by this numerical error.

resolution.summary: Evaluate the block integral correctly and enlarge the separation constant.
resolution.impact: The summable bound keeps its exponent; this repairs the cited estimate only.

entries.title: The edge-joining term in the bridge estimate
entries.locator: arXiv:2011.04642v2, section 2.4, proof of Lemma 3 (lem:2 in the e-print TeX source), HTML equation (21) and the first line of HTML equation (29) (TeX labels eq:ojs and eq:3a). Versioned HTML and e-print TeX source compared; no visual PDF check.
entries.claim: The probability that some edge of omega other than {x,y} joins [x-R,x+R) and [y-R,y+R) is bounded above by |B_R|^2 e^{-beta(K-2R)}.
entries.problem: This is not an upper bound. Each such edge has length greater than K-2R and is open with probability 1-e^{-beta/l^2}, of order beta/l^2, so the true probability is of polynomial order R^2 beta/K^2, which exceeds |B_R|^2 e^{-beta(K-2R)} for large K.
entries.correction: Replace |B_R|^2 e^{-beta(K-2R)} by |B_R|^2 (1-e^{-beta/(K-2R)^2}), which is at most |B_R|^2 beta/(K-2R)^2. The argument only needs this term to tend to 0 as K tends to infinity with R fixed, so the lemma and Theorem 1(ii) are unaffected.
entries.leanImpact: The wiki proof of 67W9 bounds the corresponding probability by 4R^2L'/(25K^2) from the tail of q and does not use the source's exponential term. No compiled declaration is supplied. The published theorem is not contradicted by this estimate.

resolution.summary: Union-bound over the |B_R|^2 possible joining edges, each of length greater than K-2R and so open with probability at most 1-e^{-beta/(K-2R)^2}.
resolution.impact: The term still tends to zero as K grows with R fixed; Lemma 3 and Theorem 1(ii) are unaffected.

versionAudit.method: The reported passages were checked in versioned HTML and extracted PDF text, as recorded in the individual locators. This summary consolidates the existing entry locators and reading records; it is not a fresh primary-text or visual-PDF audit.
versionAudit.scope: Reports are confined to the stated preprint passages. No comparison establishing whether these issues persist in the published article or a later revision is recorded here. All reports remain provisional; repair availability and Lean status are separate.
